name: Delicious Dim Sum
why: A true grab-and-go counter with cheap, fresh dumplings, which is the whole appeal. Story is close to empty: no founding date, no owners, almost no press.
story: A takeout-first dim sum shop on Jackson where locals point at trays and leave with warm paper bags. Har gow, char siu bao and lotus-leaf sticky rice are the usual haul, and it's cash only.
order: Har gow and a lotus-leaf sticky rice.
flags: Only source is an undated tourism guide. Confirm open and cash-only.
Hours on listing aggregators (about 7 am to 6 pm, closed Wednesday) are unconfirmed.
Low story score; may not earn a spot over Good Mong Kok, which is already in the guide.

name: Yasukochi's Sweet Stop
why: The last keeper of a lost San Francisco dessert, still made by the founders' grandson. Atmosphere is just a glass case in the corner of a market, which holds that mark down.
story: Thom Yasukochi learned the coffee crunch cake from Antoine, the candy maker at Blum's, the long-gone San Francisco chain that invented it. He opened this counter inside a Japantown market in 1974 to keep it alive, and a Blum's daughter later said it tasted exactly right. His grandson Kenji Yick now makes the temperamental candy topping.
order: A slice of the coffee crunch cake. Go early.
flags: Main source is from Nov 2019. Confirm it's still open, that Super Mira market is still operating, and who bakes now.
A listing mentioned a temporary closure ('open back on June 30'); year unknown.
Sell-out time (about 11:30 am) is from an undated guide; left out.
